item.title: Hokkaido Seafood Guide: Crab, Uni, Kaisendon & Where to Eat
item.description: Cold, rich northern seas make Hokkaido a paradise for seafood — arguably the best in Japan. This is the place to feast on sweet king and snow crab, melt-in-the-mouth sea urchin (uni), glistening salmon roe (ikura), plump scallops and the freshest sashimi. The signature way to enjoy it all is a kaisendon — a bowl of rice heaped with a rainbow of raw seafood — devoured at a bustling morning market.

item.title: Hokkaido Food Guide: Crab, Uni, Soup Curry, Ramen & Dairy
item.description: Hokkaido’s food culture has an unusual characteristic for Japan: it is genuinely young. The island’s large-scale settlement began in the 1870s, which means its food traditions are 150 years old — not the centuries-old layered cuisine of Kyoto or the Edo period’s Tokyo. This created a food culture that is simultaneously Japanese and something else: lamb barbecue borrowed from sheep-farming experiments, soup curry developed in a pharmacy consultation, ramen styles refined from scratch in the post-war decades, and dairy that exists because American agricultural advisors arrived in 1870 and told Hokkaido to become the dairy region of Japan.
